questions.question: What is an electrical conductor, and how can you test if a material is a conductor?
questions.expected_answer: A conductor is a material that lets electricity flow through it easily. Build a circuit with a cell, a bulb and wires, leaving a gap with a crocodile clip on each side. Clip the material into the gap. If the bulb lights, the circuit is complete and the material is a conductor.

questions.question: Which kind of materials are good conductors? Give three examples and one exception.
questions.expected_answer: Most metals are good conductors, such as copper, iron or steel, aluminium, silver, gold and brass. An exception is graphite in pencil lead, which is a non-metal that conducts. Water with dissolved substances can also conduct electricity.

questions.question: Give four reasons why copper is used for electrical wires.
questions.expected_answer: Copper is an excellent conductor, almost as good as silver. It is ductile, so it can be pulled into long, thin wires, and flexible, so it bends without snapping. It does not rust. It is much cheaper than silver or gold.
